text:
The phase margin collapse (28.6° simulated against 60.7° predicted) and the −105° sensitivity to gmid1 point to M1/M2 near the weak-inversion limit. There, a small gm/Id increase makes the pair much wider and loads node n1. Meanwhile p2 (about gm7/CL, roughly 18 MHz) sits below the UGBW, so the circuit relies on Rz cancelling p2.

The fix is to back off gmid1 and get UGBW from a smaller Cc instead. I'll also push M3/M4/M7 to higher gm/Id with shorter L, so gm7 rises without adding much node capacitance. A slightly higher i7 fixes slew and still fits in the power budget.

```json
{"action": "refine",
 "reason": "PM collapse tracks gmid1 near weak-inversion (huge M1/M2 Cdd on n1). Lower gmid1, smaller Cc keeps UGBW; raise gm7 via higher gmidp/shorter Lp and i7 (slew), keep within power (itail+1.02*i7<=27.7uA); tune kz for zero/p2 cancellation.",
 "params": {"gmid1": 19.0, "L1": 1.5, "itail": 9.5e-6, "gmidp": 16.0, "Lp": 0.5, "i7": 17.6e-6, "cc": 0.42e-12, "kz": 1.4, "rb": 10e3},
 "bounds": {"gmid1": [14.0, 22.0], "L1": [0.8, 2.5], "itail": [8.0e-6, 10.5e-6], "gmidp": [11.0, 20.0], "Lp": [0.3, 1.0], "i7": [15.5e-6, 18.0e-6], "cc": [0.3e-12, 0.6e-12], "kz": [0.8, 2.5]}}
```
